name: Gallons to Liters
title: Gallons to Liters: Volume Converter
tutorial: One US gallon is 3.78541 liters, exactly 3.785411784. The gallon is defined as 231 cubic inches, and because the inch is exactly 2.54 centimeters, the gallon in liters is exact, not approximate. Every other US volume unit is defined from the gallon, so this is the number the whole system rests on.

Gallons are the unit for big jobs in the kitchen: brining a turkey, making stock in a 12-quart pot, brewing iced tea for a crowd, or filling a water bath for canning. A 5-gallon bucket of brine is 18.93 liters. A gallon of iced tea is 3.79 liters, which is just under four 1-liter bottles.

The imperial gallon is different: 4.54609 liters, about 20 percent larger than the US gallon. A British recipe or a British fuel figure that says gallons means the bigger gallon. In the kitchen the difference matters for brines and large batches, where 20 percent is the difference between covered and dry.

Liters on this page show two decimals, so 1 gallon reads as 3.79 liters and 5 gallons as 18.93 liters. For kitchen work, 3.8 liters per gallon is a fine mental shortcut: it overshoots by less than half a percent.

The gallon ladder runs down in halves and quarters: 1 gallon is 4 quarts, 8 pints, 16 cups, and 128 fluid ounces. If a recipe gives gallons and your jug is marked in cups, multiply by 16. If it gives gallons and your pot is marked in quarts, multiply by 4.
